critical.title: AI API Key Exposure
critical.description: EXPO_PUBLIC_ prefixed AI API keys (Grok, Groq, OpenRouter) are compiled into the JavaScript bundle. Any motivated user can extract them via Hermes bytecode decompilation or runtime inspection.
critical.consequence: Unlimited API billing on your keys. Attacker can use your keys for their own applications.
critical.mitigation: Remove EXPO_PUBLIC_ AI keys from client. Proxy all AI calls through a backend API endpoint with user authentication and rate limiting. If no backend exists, disable AI features for v1 launch.

high.title: Low Test Coverage (48%)
high.description: 25+ services and 17+ engines have zero test coverage. 27 app screens have no unit or integration tests. Any refactoring or bug fix risks introducing regressions.
high.consequence: Silent bugs in production, slow development velocity, fear of changes.
high.mitigation: Priority: test subscription flow E2E, test database migrations, test workout generation edge cases. Target 70% service coverage.

high.title: Health Connect Crashes
high.description: Health Connect integration (react-native-health-connect) causes app crashes. Feature flag ff_health_sync is disabled. Android users cannot sync health data from Google Fit or Samsung Health.
high.consequence: Major feature gap on Android. Competitors offer this. User reviews will mention it.
high.mitigation: Debug crashes in isolation. Wrap Health Connect calls in try/catch + error boundaries. Enable behind feature flag for beta testers first.

high.title: No Push Notifications
high.description: expo-notifications plugin is configured but no notification scheduling logic exists. No streak reminders, trial expiry warnings, or re-engagement nudges.
high.consequence: Poor retention. Users forget about the app. Trial expires silently without urgency.
high.mitigation: Implement local notification scheduling: daily workout reminder, streak at risk (missed 1 day), trial countdown (days 10, 12, 13, 14).

high.title: 58 react-hooks/exhaustive-deps Violations
high.description: 58 hooks with missing or incorrect dependency arrays. Each is a potential stale closure bug — the component reads old state/props when it should read current ones.
high.consequence: Intermittent UI bugs, stale data display, effects that don't re-run when they should.
high.mitigation: Audit each violation manually. Most are intentional (stable refs), but some are genuine bugs. Fix genuine bugs, add eslint-disable with comments for intentional ones.

high.title: Silent Error Suppression
high.description: 20+ locations use .catch(() => {}) to silently swallow errors. Most are in database service.ts (WAL failure marking), AI providers, and background engines.
high.consequence: Data operations fail silently. Database corruption goes undetected. AI conversations lost without user knowing.
high.mitigation: Replace all .catch(() => {}) with .catch(e => logError(e, { context: 'operation_name' })). Keep fire-and-forget pattern but log the failure.

medium.title: No Cross-Device Sync
medium.description: All data lives on-device. No server means no sync between devices. Cloud backup exists but is manual and requires EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKUP_API_BASE_URL to be configured.
medium.consequence: Users lose data on device change/loss unless they manually export. Premium subscribers expect cloud sync.
medium.mitigation: Phase 12: Implement lightweight backend (Cloudflare Workers + D1) for encrypted sync. In the interim, make backup flow more prominent in UI.

medium.title: No Root/Jailbreak Detection
medium.description: App runs without restriction on rooted Android or jailbroken iOS devices. SQLite database and SecureStore are accessible to other processes.
medium.consequence: Database tampering, subscription bypass, encryption key extraction on compromised devices.
medium.mitigation: Add root detection library. Warn users on compromised devices. Consider restricting encrypted features.

medium.title: No Certificate Pinning
medium.description: Network calls to RevenueCat, PostHog, Sentry, and AI providers use default TLS without certificate pinning.
medium.consequence: Man-in-the-middle attacks can intercept API keys, analytics data, and subscription receipts.
medium.mitigation: Implement certificate pinning for RevenueCat and AI provider endpoints. Lower priority since all sensitive data is encrypted at rest.

medium.title: Large Screen Files (1000+ lines)
medium.description: fitquest.tsx, dashboard.tsx, profile.tsx, and several other screens exceed 1000 lines with complex state management, multiple useEffects, and inline logic.
medium.consequence: Difficult to debug, high cognitive load, merge conflicts, slow code review.
medium.mitigation: Extract sub-components, move business logic to hooks, split into composition pattern.

medium.title: PostHog Session Replay May Capture Health Data
medium.description: PostHog session replay (posthog-react-native-session-replay) captures screen content. Health dashboard, encrypted data screens may have sensitive information visible.
medium.consequence: GDPR/HIPAA concern if health data is transmitted to PostHog servers.
medium.mitigation: Configure session replay masking for health-related screens. Audit PostHog data collection scope.

low.title: Apollo Client Dead Dependency
low.description: @apollo/client is installed but never used (SQLite is sole data source). Adds ~150KB to bundle.

low.title: No Bundle Size Monitoring
low.description: No automated bundle size tracking in CI. 56 production dependencies without size analysis.
low.mitigation: Add expo-optimize or custom size tracking to CI pipeline.

low.title: 275 Unused Variables
low.description: 275 no-unused-vars warnings. Most are unused imports or destructured variables.
low.mitigation: Systematic cleanup. Can be partially automated with ESLint --fix and unused imports plugin.

top_3_actions: 1. Remove AI API keys from client bundle OR proxy through backend (SEC-H1, RISK-C1)
2. Replace silent .catch(() => {}) with error telemetry logging (RISK-H5)
3. Implement local push notifications for retention (RISK-H3)
